text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek will open a two-day conference on investment opportunities in the Central European Free Trade Area (CEFTA) in New York on Monday.
- According to an opinion poll, the most popular politician in Slovenia is President Milan Kucan, followed by Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek and Parliamentary Speaker Janez Podobnik.
- Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler on Monday starts a six-day diplomatic trip to the Council of Europe, Denmark and Iceland.

- About 29.9 percent of Slovenians support the centre-left Liberal Democratic Party of Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, followed by the conservative People's Party, which enjoys the support of 10.6 percent of citizens, an opinion poll showed.

- Over the next three years Slovenia will change about 80 laws to comply with the regulations of the European Union. Slovenia signed an association accord with the EU in June 1996 and hopes to become a full member as soon as possible.
- Slovenia's only nuclear power plant Krsko has not yet determined where it will deposit two steam generators, which will be raplaced by new ones presumably in 1999.
- Hotels at the Slovenian seaside were fully booked over the Labour Day holidays which started last Thursday.
- A total of 232 Slovenian companies have been awarded the international quality standard ISO 9001.
